A: Susan B. Anthony and Thomas Joseph Drury met in 1890 when Anthony spoke at a political meeting at the Warner Opera House in Ludington. Anthony delivered a speech entitled, “Our Country’s Need,” in support of the suffrage movement. She made three requests of her audience. First, she asked them to work toward political equality. Second, she asked for them to increase their education and use it to benefit society as a whole. Third, she asked them to vote.
